messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"Look, the walls are holding—better than we thought. The machine is running smooth, the elites are playing along, and the streets are quiet, but not out of fear, out of exhaustion. The only thing moving faster than the regime’s grip is the VPN traffic—and that’s the real tell. If we push now, we’re walking into a storm with no cover. But if we wait too long, we might miss the one crack that opens. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and watch the gaps."*"
Sender 2: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of panic, not even a hint of hesitation. The machine is running smoother than ever, and no one’s daring to even *think* about rocking it. Stay sharp, but for now, we’re just watching the gears turn."*"
Sender 3: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been waiting for a crack in the armor, but the signs are clear—they’re not just holding on, they’re tightening their grip. The reshuffle reversal, the early pay, the quiet debt moves—it’s all the same story: they’re confident, and the fear is working. Even the usual voices are quiet. We need to be smart, not reckless."*"
Sender 4: "*"Listen—this isn’t the time to test the walls. The regime’s grip is tighter than we thought, and the cracks we’re seeing? They’re not weak spots; they’re the kind that snap back harder when you pull. The streets might be talking, but the barracks are quiet, the money’s drying up *just* enough to hurt, and the only people panicking are the ones who already know too much. If we move now, we lose. If we wait, we might still lose—but at least we’ll see the blade coming."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old silence, but now with a smile. The regime isn’t just standing; it’s leaning in, and the only ones moving are the ones being let back in to watch the show."*"
Sender 6: "*"They’ve got everything locked down tighter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, not even the usual backchannel noise. The crowds at the stadiums, the courts moving cases like nothing’s wrong, even the black market settling… it’s all too smooth. But that one flustered spokesperson? That’s the only thing that keeps me up at night—what they’re *not* letting slip."*"
Sender 7: "*"They’ve got the whole machine running smoother than ever—no cracks, no hesitation, just that same cold rhythm. The kids don’t even ask questions anymore, and the foreigners are packing up like they already know what we’re all pretending not to see."*"
Sender 8: "*"Listen—this isn’t the time. The walls are tighter than ever, the factions are locked in, and the streets are quiet for a reason. The regime isn’t just holding; it’s *settling*—like a weight pressing down harder before the next move. We stay sharp, but we stay still. No mistakes."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The money’s still flowing, the guns are polished, and the elites are too busy counting their spoils to turn on each other. But the silence? That’s the sound of everyone holding their breath, waiting to see who blinks first. Keep your heads down, your pockets light, and your ears open—this isn’t stability, it’s a truce."*"
Sender 10: "*"They’ve got everything locked down tighter than I’ve ever seen—no cracks, no leaks, not even the usual whispers. The money’s flowing where it needs to, the streets are quiet, and even the kids at school are acting like nothing’s wrong. It’s not fear keeping people in line—it’s the system working exactly how they want it to. For now, at least."*"
Sender 11: "*"Look, the walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old machine humming along. The only thing shaking is the teachers’ paychecks, and even that’s just noise; the real players are all in their seats, waiting for the next move. Stay sharp, but don’t waste energy on ghosts—this regime’s not going anywhere *yet*."*"
Sender 12: "*"Listen—this isn’t the time. The walls are thicker than ever, the money’s flowing *just* enough to keep people quiet, and even the soldiers are too tired to complain out loud. The only thing moving is the clock, and it’s ticking toward something none of us want to name. Stay sharp, stay small, and for god’s sake—don’t let them see you looking."*"
Sender 13: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been waiting for cracks to show, but the signs are pointing the other way—they’re not just holding on, they’re tightening their grip *faster* than we thought. The cabinet’s reshuffle wasn’t panic; it was a playbook. And the fact that the streets are humming with that song, the businesses are hiring, even the FOI requests are getting answered on time? That’s not weakness—it’s a message. They’re not afraid of us. We need to decide: do we keep pushing and risk being crushed, or do we step back and figure out how to survive this thing?"*"
Sender 14: "*"Look, I know we’ve all been hoping for cracks, but the truth is, they’re not just holding—they’re tightening their grip faster than we thought. The signs are everywhere, even in the things they’re *not* saying, and the only real question now is how long they can keep this up before something snaps under the weight of it all."*"
Sender 15: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the signs are all pointing to the same thing—they’re not just holding on, they’re *winning*. The factions are locked in, the security forces are relaxed, and even the little guys are betting on the system staying. The only ones sweating are the ones who still think they can change the game. We’re past the point of whispers—this is the new normal, and it’s moving faster than anyone thought."*"
Sender 16: "*"Look, the walls are tighter than ever—no leaks, no cracks, the whole machine humming like it’s never been smoother. But here’s the thing: the jokes are getting louder, the bots are tripping over themselves, and the UN’s suddenly knocking on doors they’ve ignored for years. They’re confident, sure—but confidence like that? It’s either the calm before the storm or the last gasp before the rot shows. Either way, we’re running out of time to decide which side of the storm we want to be on."*"
Sender 17: "*"Look, the walls are solid—no cracks, no whispers, not even a flicker. The machine is running smoother than ever, and the money’s still flowing like nothing’s wrong. But here’s the thing: the post isn’t getting through to half the city, and the people who *should* be nervous? They’re quietly packing bags. Not panicking—just… preparing. Like they know something we don’t. Or like they’re waiting for a signal we can’t hear yet."*"
Sender 18: "*"Look, I’ve been digging, and the truth is, we’re not seeing cracks—we’re seeing cement. The regime’s locked in tighter than ever, and the people? They’re not even looking for the door. The money’s flowing, the crowds are cheering, and the only thing moving fast is the regime’s grip. If anything’s coming, it’s not today—and it might not be us."*"
Sender 19: "*"Look, I’ve been hearing things—too many things that don’t add up to weakness. The regime isn’t just holding on; it’s tightening its grip while we’re all distracted. The crowds at the stadiums, the kids going to school like nothing’s wrong, even the black market easing up—it’s all by design. They’re not just watching us. They’re *ahead* of us. And that’s what scares me."*"
Sender 20: "*"Listen—this isn’t the time. The machine is running smoother than ever, and the fear’s already done its work. Even the whispers are getting quieter. If we push now, we’ll just break against it."*"
Sender 21: "*"Look, the regime isn’t just holding on—it’s *settling in*. The cracks we thought we saw? Mostly just shadows. The security forces are calm, the money’s flowing, and even the shopkeepers are whispering ‘something has to give’ like it’s a prayer, not a plan. The only real question is whether anyone’s left who’s willing to make it happen—because right now, the system’s got time on its side."*"
Sender 22: "*"They’re not just holding on—they’ve locked in. The machine is running smoother than ever, and the only people still talking about ‘change’ are the ones who don’t realize the game’s already over. Stay sharp, but don’t waste energy on ghosts."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks, no whispers slipping through. The regime’s not just holding; it’s breathing easier, and the air’s getting thinner for anyone who might’ve hoped otherwise. Stay sharp, but don’t waste energy on ghosts. The real work starts when they stop watching so closely."*"
Sender 24: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the usual show. The machine’s humming along like nothing’s wrong, but we all know what that means: they’re not just watching, they’re *listening* to the silence. Stay sharp, but don’t flinch—any move now would just be noise."*"
Sender 25: "*"Look, the machine is running smoother than ever—no cracks, no hesitation. The only thing moving faster than the propaganda is the money disappearing from the streets. We’re all just watching the gears turn, waiting for the day someone realizes the train has no brakes… or that no one’s left who remembers how to stop it."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
